questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A man who wears glasses of power 3D must holds a newspaper at least 25 cm away to see the print clearly. How far away would the newspaper have to be if he took off the glasses and still wanted clear vision?
questions.solution:
Given, power $P=3 Df=\frac{1}{P}=\frac{1}{3} \mathrm{~m}=\frac{100}{3} \mathrm{~cm}$.
$u=-25 \mathrm{~cm}$
Applying lens formula, we can write
$\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{25}=\frac{3}{100}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{v}=\frac{3}{100}-\frac{1}{25}=\frac{3-4}{100}=\frac{-1}{100}v=-100 \mathrm{~cm}$
Now, again using lens formula we can write
$\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}$
As, focal length of a far sighted person deceases
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{-100}-\frac{1}{u}\gt\frac{1}{1.7}=\frac{10}{17} \quad[\because f \lt 1.7 \mathrm{~cm}]\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & \frac{1}{u} \lt \frac{-1}{100}-\frac{10}{17} \\ & =\frac{-17-1000}{1700}=\frac{-1017}{1700}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow u\gt\frac{1700}{1000} \approx-1.7=-1 \mathrm{~m}$ (nearest option)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnifying power of a telescope is $m^{\prime}$. If the focal length of the eye piece is doubled, then its magnifying power will become
questions.solution:
Magnifying power of a telescope is given by
$m=\frac{f_o}{f_e}$
If the focal length of the eye piece is doubled, the new magnifying power is given by
$m^{\prime}=\frac{f_o}{f_e^{\prime}}=\frac{f_o}{2 f_e}\therefore \quad m^{\prime}=\frac{m}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A concave lens is kept in contact with a convex lens of focal length 20 cm . The combination works as convex lens of focal length 50 cm . The power of concave lens is
questions.solution:
Power of the combination
$P=P_1+P_2=P_{\text {concave }}+P_{\text {convex }}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{100}{50}=P_{\text {concave }}+\frac{100}{20}$
or $\quad 2=P_{\text {concave }}+5$
or $\quad P_{\text {concave }}=2-5=-3.0 \mathrm{D}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}}, \overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{C}}$ are the unit vectors along the incident ray, reflected ray and outward normal to the reflecting surface, then:
questions.solution:
Let $\vec{A}, \vec{B}$ and $\vec{C}$ be as shown in figure. Let $\theta$ be the angle of incidence, which is equal to the angle of reflection. Resolving these vectors in rectangular components, we have

$\begin{aligned} \overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}} & =\sin \theta \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\cos \theta \hat{\mathbf{j}} \\ \overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}} & =\sin \theta \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\cos \theta \hat{\mathbf{j}} \\ \overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}-\overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}} & =2 \cos \theta \hat{\mathbf{j}}\end{aligned}$ or $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}=\overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}}+2 \cos \theta \hat{\mathbf{j}}$ Now, $\quad \overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathbf{C}}=(1)(1) \cos \left(180^{\circ}-\theta\right)=-\cos \theta\therefore \quad \vec{B}=\vec{A}-2(\vec{A} \cdot \vec{C}) \hat{j}$ or $\vec{B}=\overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}}-2(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathbf{C}}) \overrightarrow{\mathbf{C}}($ as $\hat{j}=\overrightarrow{\mathbf{C}})$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The angle of a prism is $A$. One of its refracting surface is silvered. If light rays: falling at an angle of incidence $2 A$ on the first suface returns back through the same path ater reflection from silvered surface. The refractive index $\mu$ of the prism is
questions.solution:
If reflected ray from silvered surface retrace its path, then it falls normally on the silvered surface.
$\therefore$ From the geometry, $\begin{aligned} & i=2 A, r=A \\ \therefore \quad \mu & =\text { Refractive index }=\frac{\sin i}{\sin r} \text { (From Snell's law) } \\ & =\frac{\sin 2 A}{\sin A}=\frac{2 \sin A \cdot \cos A}{\sin A} \\ & =2 \cos A \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a lens is cut into two halves along $X O X^{\prime}$, then focal length of each half lens
questions.solution:
If $R$ be the magnitude of radius of curvature of equiconvex lens, then its focal length $f$ is given by
$\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{f} & =(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right) \\
& =(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{R}-\frac{1}{-R}\right)=\frac{2(\mu-1)}{R} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{1}{f} & =\frac{2(\mu-1)}{R}...(i)
\end{aligned}$
When equiconvex lens is cut into two halves along $X O X^{\prime}$, then
$R_1=R, R_2=-R\therefore$ Focal length $f^{\prime}$ is given as
$\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{f^{\prime}} & =(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{R}-\frac{1}{-R}\right)=\frac{2(\mu-1)}{R}=\frac{1}{f} \quad[\text { from (i) }] \\
\Rightarrow  f^{\prime} & =f
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In the formation of a rainbow light from the sun on water droplets undergoes
questions.solution: Rainbow occurs in the form of concentric colourd circular arcs in the sky, when the sun shines on rain drops during or after the shower. This phenomenon occurs due to combined effect of dispersion, refraction and total internal reflection of sunlight by spherical drop of water.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A light ray from air is incident (as shown in figure) at one end of a glass fiber (refractive index, $\mu=1.5$ ) making an incidence angle of $60^{\circ}$ on the lateral surface, so that it undergoes a total internal reflection. How much time would it take to traverse the straight fiber of length 1 km ?
questions.solution:
Velocity of light in fiber $v=\frac{c}{\mu}=\frac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5}=2 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
Straight length is 1 km , Distance covered by light, $s=\frac{1 \mathrm{~km}}{\sin 60^{\circ}}=\frac{1000}{\sqrt{3} / 2}=\frac{2000}{\sqrt{3}}$
So, time taken $=\frac{s}{v}=\frac{2000 / \sqrt{3}}{2 \times 10^8}=3.85 \mu \mathrm{~s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light travelling from a transparent medium to air undergoes total internal reflection at an angle of incidence of $45^{\circ}$. Then refractive index of the medium may be
questions.solution:
At $45^{\circ}$ total internal reflection takes place so, critical angle, $C=45^{\circ}$.
Refractive index, $\mu=\frac{1}{\sin C}=\frac{1}{\sin 45^{\circ}}\begin{aligned}
& =\sqrt{2}=1.414 \\
& \approx 1.5
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If refractive index of a material of equilateral prism is $\sqrt{3}$, then angle of minimum deviation of the prism is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned}  \mu & =\frac{\sin \left(\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin \frac{A}{2}} \\ \sqrt{3} & =\frac{\sin \left(\frac{60^{\circ}+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin \frac{60^{\circ}}{2}} \Rightarrow \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\sin \left[30^{\circ}+\frac{\delta_m}{2}\right] \\ \Rightarrow \delta_m & =60^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The angle of a prism is $60^{\circ}$ and its refractive index is $\sqrt{2}$. The angle of minimum deviation suffered by a ray of light in passing through it is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Refractive index, } \mu=\frac{\sin \left(\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin \left(\frac{A}{2}\right)} \\ \Rightarrow  & \sqrt{2}=\frac{\sin \left(\frac{60^{\circ}+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin \left(\frac{60^{\circ}}{2}\right)} \\ \Rightarrow  & \sqrt{2} \times \sin 30^{\circ}=\sin \left(\frac{60^{\circ}+\delta_m}{2}\right) \\ \Rightarrow  & \sin 45^{\circ}=\sin \left(\frac{60^{\circ}+\delta_m}{2}\right) \\ \Rightarrow  & \delta_m=30^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The plane faces of two identical plano-convex lenses each having a focal length of 50 cm are placed against each other to form a usual biconvex lens. The distance from this lens combination at which an object must be placed to obtain a real, inverted image which has the same size as the object is
questions.solution:
The focal length of the combination is
$\frac{1}{F}=\frac{1}{f_1}+\frac{1}{f_2}\begin{array}{ll}
\text { Given, } & f_1=50 \mathrm{~cm}, f_2=50 \mathrm{~cm} \\
\therefore & \frac{1}{F}=\frac{1}{50}+\frac{1}{50}=\frac{2}{50} \\
\Rightarrow & F=\frac{50}{2}=25 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{array}$
Object when placed at centre of curvature forms a real, inverted image of same size as object $=(2 \times 25=50 \mathrm{~cm})$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A thin rod of length $\frac{f}{3}$ is placed along the optic axis of a concave mirror of focal length $f$, such that its image which is real and elongated just touches the rod, the magnification is
questions.solution:
$u=P A=P C-A C=2 f-\frac{f}{3}=\frac{5 f}{3}$

From mirror formula $\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}-\frac{3}{5 f}=\frac{2}{5 f}$ Length of image $C A^{\prime}=P A^{\prime}-P C=\frac{5 f}{2}-2 f=\frac{f}{2}\therefore$ Magnification $(m)=\frac{C A^{\prime}}{C A}=\frac{f / 2}{f / 3}=1.5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The angle of minimum deviation for a prism of angle $A$ is $180-2 A$. The refractive index is
questions.solution:
Refractive index is given by
$n=\frac{\sin \left(\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin \frac{A}{2}}$
Given, $\delta_m=180^{\circ}-2 \mathrm{~A}\begin{aligned}
\therefore & n=\frac{\sin \left(\frac{A+180^{\circ}-2 A}{2}\right)}{\sin \frac{A}{2}} \\
& n=\frac{\sin \left(\frac{180^{\circ}}{2}-\frac{A}{2}\right)}{\sin \frac{A}{2}} \\
\Rightarrow & n=\frac{\cos \frac{A}{2}}{\sin \frac{A}{2}}=\cot \frac{A}{2} .
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: White light reflected at normal incidence from a soap film has minima at $6500 Å$ and maxima at $7500 Å$ in the visible region with not minimum in between. If $\mu$ is $\frac{5}{3}$ for the, thin film, the thickness of film is
questions.solution:
For minima to occur,
$2 \mu t=2 n \frac{\lambda_1}{2}\ldots$ (i)
and for maxima
$2 \mu t=(2 n-1) \frac{\lambda_2}{2}\ldots$ (ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$(2 n-1) \lambda_2=2 n \lambda_1$
or $\quad(2 n-1) 7500=(2 n) 6500$
[given, $\lambda_2=7500 Å, \lambda_1=6500 Å$ ]
or $1500 n-7500=13000 n$
or $2000 n=7500$
or $n=3.75$
Substitution the value of ($n$) in Eq. (i), we get
$2 \times \frac{5}{3} \times t=2 \times 3.75 \times \frac{6500}{2} \times 10^{-10} \quad\left[\because \mu=\frac{5}{3}\right]\Rightarrow \quad t=7.40 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A ray of light is travelling through a medium of refractive index $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ with respect to air.
When it is incident on the surface making an angle $45^{\circ}$ with the surface, which of the following will take place?
options: The ray will be internally reflected
questions.solution:
Given, $\mu=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ w.r.t. air $i=45^{\circ}, r=$ ?
Also, $\mu=\frac{\sin i}{\sin r}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{\sin 45^{\circ}}{\sin r} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1 / \sqrt{2}}{\sin r}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & & \sin r & =1 \\ \Rightarrow & & r & =90^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
Note that the ray is incident from denser medium and is refracted into a rarer medium air.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A thin walled glass sphere of radius 2.5 cm is filled with water. An object $(O)$ is placed at 7.5 cm from the surface of the sphere. Neglecting the effect of glass wall, at what distance the image ( $I$ ) of the object, measured from the centre of sphere is formed?
questions.solution:
For refraction at first surface,
$u=-7.5 \mathrm{~cm}, R_1=2.5 \mathrm{~cm}\mu_1=1, \mu_2=\frac{4}{3}\therefore \quad \frac{\mu_2}{v^{\prime}}-\frac{\mu_1}{u}=\frac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R_1}\frac{4 / 3}{v^{\prime}}-\frac{1}{(-7.5)}=\frac{4 / 3-1}{25}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{4}{3 v^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{7.5}-\frac{1}{7.5}=0\Rightarrow \quad v^{\prime}=\infty$
It means the ray is parallel within the sphere. For refraction at second surface,
$u=-\infty, \mu_1=\frac{4}{3}\mu_2=1, R_2=-2.5 \mathrm{~cm}\therefore \quad \frac{\mu_2}{v^{\prime}}-\frac{\mu_1}{u}=\frac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R_2}$ gives
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{v^{\prime}}-\frac{4 / 3}{(-\infty)}=\frac{1-(4 / 3)}{(-2.5)}\Rightarrow \quad v=+7.5 \mathrm{~cm}$
i.e. Image is formed at distance 7.5 cm to the right of $P_2$. Hence, distance of final image $P$ from centre $C=7.5+2.5=10 \mathrm{~cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Figure shows an irregular block of material of refractive index $\sqrt{2}$. A ray of light strikes the face $A B$ as shown in figure. After refraction, it is incident on a spherical surface $C D$ of radius of curvature 0.4 m and enters a medium of refractive index 1.514 to meet $P Q$ at $E$. Find the distance $O E$ upto two places of decimal.
questions.solution:
From Snell's law,
$\begin{aligned} & \mu_1 \sin i & =\mu_2 \sin r \\ \Rightarrow & \sin r=\frac{\mu_1}{\mu_2} \sin i & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin 45^{\circ} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \frac{1}{2}=\sin r & \Rightarrow r=30^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
This means that the ray becomes parallel to side $A D$ inside the slab.
This implies for the second face $C D, u=\infty$.
Given
$\begin{aligned}
R & =0.1 \mathrm{m} \\
\frac{\mu_3}{v}-\frac{\mu_2}{v} & =\frac{\mu_3-\mu_2}{R}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1.514}{v}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\infty} & =\frac{1.514-\sqrt{2}}{R} \\ v & =\frac{1.514 \times 0.4}{1.514-1.414}=\frac{1.514 \times 0.4}{0.1} \\ v=6.056 & =6.06 \mathrm{~m} \text { (upto } 2 \text { decimal places) }\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rectangular glass slab $A B C D$ of refractive index $n_1$ is immersed in water of refractive index $n_2\left(n_1 \gt n_2\right)$. A ray of light is incident at the surface $A B$ of the slab as shown. The maximum value of the angle of incidence $\alpha_{\max }$ such that the ray comes out only from the another surface $C D$ is given by
questions.solution:
Rays comes out only from $C D$, means rays after refraction from $A B$ get totally internally reflected at $A D$.
From the figure, $\begin{aligned} r_1+r_2 & =90 \\ r_1 & =90-r_2 \\ \left(r_1\right)_{\max } & =90^{\circ}-\left(r_2\right)_{\max } \text { and }\left(r_2\right)_{\min }=\theta_C \end{aligned}$ (for total internal reflection at $A D$ ) where, $\quad \sin \theta_C=\frac{n_2}{n_1}$ or $\theta_C=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{n_2}{n_1}\right)\therefore \quad\left(r_1\right)_{\max }=90^{\circ}-\theta_C$ Now, applying Snell's law at face $A B$, we wet $\begin{gathered}\frac{n_1}{n_2}=\frac{\sin \alpha_{\max }}{\sin \left(r_1\right)_{\max }}=\frac{\sin \alpha_{\max }}{\sin \left(90-\theta_C\right)}=\frac{\sin \alpha_{\max }}{\cos \theta_C} \\ \sin \alpha_{\max }=\frac{n_1}{n_2} \cos \theta_C\end{gathered}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \alpha_{\max } & =\sin ^{-1}\left[\frac{n_1}{n_2} \cos \theta_C\right] \\ & =\sin ^{-1}\left[\frac{n_1}{n_2} \cos \left(\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{n_2}{n_1}\right)\right)\right]\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A point object $O$ is placed in front of a glass rod having spherical end of radius of curvature 30 cm . The image would be formed at
questions.solution:
Focal length of glass rod, $f=\frac{R}{2}=\frac{30}{2}=15 \mathrm{~cm}$
Distance of object, $u=-15 \mathrm{~cm}$ From formula, $\begin{aligned} \frac{\mu_2}{v}-\frac{\mu_1}{u} & =\frac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R} \\ \mu_2 & =1.5 \quad \text { (for glass) } \\ \mu_1 & =1 \quad \text { (for air) } \\ \frac{1.3}{v} & =-\frac{1}{-15}=\frac{1.5-1}{30} \\ \frac{1.5}{v}+\frac{1}{15} & =\frac{0.5}{30} \\ \frac{1.5}{v} & =\frac{1}{60}-\frac{1}{15} \\ \frac{1.5}{v} & =\frac{-1}{20} \\ v & =-30 \mathrm{~cm} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A man at a distance 11 km from two pillars wants to see two pillars separately. What will be the approximate distance between the pillars?
questions.solution:
Resolving power of eye $=\left(\frac{1}{60}\right)^{\circ}=\frac{1}{60} \times \frac{\pi}{180}$
Let the minimum distance between the poles be $d$,
then, $\frac{d}{11000}=\frac{1}{60} \times \frac{\pi}{180}$
or $\quad d=11000 \times \frac{1}{60} \times \frac{\pi}{180}=3 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.q: Graph of position of image versus position of point object from a convex lens is shown. Then, focal length of the lens is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u} \Rightarrow f & =5 \mathrm{~cm} \\ f & =\frac{u v}{u+v} \\ \frac{\Delta f}{f} & =\left|\frac{\Delta u}{u}\right|+\left|\frac{\Delta v}{v}\right|+\frac{|\Delta u|+|\Delta v|}{|u|+|v|} \\ \Delta f & =0.15 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A thin prism $P_1$ of angle $4^{\circ}$ and refractive index $1.54^{\circ}$ is combined with another thin prism $P_2$ of refractive index 1.72 to produce dispersion without deviation. The angle of $P_2$ is
questions.solution:
Angle of deviation $\delta=(n-1) A$.
Dispersion produced by both the prism's will be equal.
$\begin{aligned}\left(n_1-1\right) A_1 & =\left(n_2-1\right) A_2 \\ \Rightarrow \quad A_2= & \frac{\left(n_1-1\right) A_1}{\left(n_2-1\right)}=\frac{(1.54-1)}{(1.72-1)}=3^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
Hence, the angle of prism $P_2$ is $3^{\circ}$.

questions.q: A prism of refractive index $\sqrt{2}$ has refracting angle of $60^{\circ}$. At what angle a ray must be incident one it so that it suffers a minimum deviation?
questions.solution:
In the position of minimum deviation angle of incidence is equal to angle of emergence. Let a ray of monochromatic light $P Q$ be incident on face $A B . P Q R S$ is path of light ray,
where $i$ is angle of incidence $r$ angle of refraction, $r$ angle of incidence and $i$ angle of emergence. In position of minimum deviation $i^{\prime}=i, r^{\prime}=r, \delta=\delta m2 r=A$ or $r=\frac{A}{2}$ Given $A=60^{\circ}$, $r=\frac{60^{\circ}}{2}=30^{\circ}$ Also from Snell's law $\mu=\frac{\sin i}{\sin r}=\frac{\sin i}{\sin 30^{\circ}}\sqrt{2}=\frac{\sin i}{\sin 30^{\circ}}\Rightarrow \quad \sin i=\sqrt{2} \times \frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\Rightarrow \quad i=45^{\circ}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A fish at a depth of 12 cm in water is viewed by an observer on the bank of a lake. To what height the image of the fish is raised?
(Refractive index of lake water $=\frac{4}{3}$ )
questions.solution: Apparent rise $=d\left(1-\frac{1}{a \mu_w}\right)\begin{aligned} & =12 \times\left(1-\frac{3}{4}\right) \\ & =12 \times \frac{1}{4}=3 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The angle of minimum deviation $\delta_m$ for an equilateral glass prism is $30^{\circ}$. Refractive index of the prism is
questions.solution:
$A=60^{\circ}, \delta_m=30^{\circ}$
As $\mu=\sin \frac{\left(\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin \left(\frac{A}{2}\right)}\therefore  \mu=\sin \frac{\frac{\left(60^{\circ}+30^{\circ}\right)}{2}}{\sin \left(\frac{60^{\circ}}{2}\right)}=\frac{\sin 45^{\circ}}{\sin 30^{\circ}}=\frac{1 / \sqrt{2}}{1 / 2}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}$

questions.q: When a glass prism of refracting angle $60^{\circ}$ is immersed in a liquid its angle of minimum deviation is $30^{\circ}$. The critical angle of glass with respect to the liquid medium is
questions.solution:
Given, $A=60^{\circ}$ and $\delta_m=30^{\circ}$
So, $\mu=\frac{\sin \left(\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin \frac{A}{2}}=\frac{\sin \left(\frac{60^{\circ}+30^{\circ}}{2}\right)}{\sin \frac{60^{\circ}}{2}}=\frac{\sin 45^{\circ}}{\sin 30^{\circ}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times 2=\frac{2 \times \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2}}=\frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{2}=\sqrt{2}$
We have, $\mu=\frac{1}{\sin C}$
or $\quad \sqrt{2}=\frac{1}{\sin C}$
or $\quad C=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)=45^{\circ}$
